cohort: The study included pregnant mothers and their babies, observing their maternal diet during pregnancy and subsequent birth outcomes.
finding: Maternal diet during pregnancy showed a significant relationship with both the baby's birth length (p=0.004) and birth weight (p=0.000).
cross-section timing: Maternal diet was assessed retrospectively for pregnancy, and baby's birth length and weight were measured at birth.
birth_weight: 91.1% of babies had normal birth weight and 8.9% had low birth weight, while 85.6% had normal birth length and 14.4% had short birth length.
